answer: Drop one anchor per ballot and watch it swing. Each ballot is a boat at anchor: it logs its GPS fix each ten minutes through one tide, tracing the spiral its hull draws as wind and current shift, plus one bearing to a mark on the horizon. A farm dies by the swing check: two ballots whose swing circles share one anchor centre within 5 metres are both cut loose, stakes slashed. Faking 10,000 ballots takes 10,000 anchors and 200,000 metres of chain at $3 a metre — $600,000 of steel — and $25 staked per ballot locks $250,000 more away. Ten thousand boats on one hook drag each other down.
